title: EU Battery Regulation: recycling targets and recycled-content quotas
text: The regulation sets binding collection targets for waste batteries and minimum recycled-content quotas for cobalt, lithium and nickel in new industrial and EV batteries. Producers carry extended responsibility for end-of-life treatment. Recovery targets for lithium rise stepwise, and compliance is documented through a digital battery passport. The staged timeline gives European recyclers a predictable demand signal for recycled battery materials through the next decade.

title: Hydrometallurgical recycling of lithium-ion batteries: a review
text: This review compares pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical routes for lithium-ion battery recycling. Hydrometallurgical processes recover lithium, cobalt and nickel at high purity with lower energy input, but are sensitive to feedstock variability and reagent costs. Reported lithium recovery rates in pilot plants range from 50 to 90 percent; published figures are often not comparable because system boundaries differ. European pilot capacity is growing from a small base.

title: GreenVolt press release: our recycling breakthrough changes everything
text: GreenVolt announces a proprietary battery recycling process with, the company states, 99 percent lithium recovery at half the cost of any competitor. Internal projections show GreenVolt capturing a third of the European recycling market within three years. The figures come from company-run trials and have not been independently verified. Analysts quoted in the release are retained by GreenVolt. Investors are invited to the upcoming funding round.

title: Washington Battery Policy Institute: America's recycling edge
text: The institute argues that federal tax credits give the United States a durable advantage in battery recycling and lithium refining over European and Asian competitors. It recommends tighter export controls on black mass and expanded subsidies for domestic processors. The report is well documented, but its policy recommendations and framing reflect the institute's stated mission of advancing US industrial competitiveness in the battery supply chain.

title: European Raw Materials Alliance briefing: lithium supply for Europe
text: Europe consumes a growing share of global lithium but refines very little of it. The briefing maps announced European extraction and refining projects, from geothermal brine in the Rhine valley to hard-rock projects in Iberia, and estimates that even under optimistic scenarios domestic supply covers well under half of European demand by 2030. Recycled lithium becomes a strategically relevant secondary source only after 2030, when volumes of end-of-life EV batteries rise.

title: Global lithium supply chains: geological and geopolitical constraints
text: Lithium extraction is concentrated in Australia, Chile and China, while refining capacity is overwhelmingly Chinese. The paper models supply under demand scenarios to 2035 and finds that bottlenecks sit in refining and qualification, not geology. Diversification through new mines takes seven to ten years from discovery to production. Recycling eases but does not remove import dependence for fast-growing markets such as the European Union.
